culture.title: Sri Mariamman Temple in Chinatown
culture.description: The oldest Hindu temple in Singapore, built in 1827 by immigrants from the Coromandel Coast, with a gopuram of painted deities in the middle of Chinatown.
culture.bonus: Take your shoes off, walk the inner corridor and look up at the ceiling.

culture.title: Asian Civilisations Museum by the River
culture.description: A riverside museum organised by trade route rather than country, with a shipwreck gallery of ninth-century Tang cargo pulled from the Java Sea.
culture.bonus: Go straight to the Tang shipwreck gallery and start there.

culture.title: Contemporary Art at SAM, Tanjong Pagar
culture.description: The Singapore Art Museum's warehouse galleries inside a working port distripark, showing large-scale Southeast Asian contemporary work.
culture.bonus: Have a coffee upstairs and watch the container cranes through the window.

culture.title: ArtScience Museum at Marina Bay
culture.description: The lotus-shaped museum on the bay that collects rainwater through its own roof, running shows where the art and the engineering are the same thing.
culture.bonus: Go to the top of the central atrium and look straight up through the petals.

culture.title: National Museum of Singapore
culture.description: The country's oldest museum, in a domed 1887 building, telling 700 years of the island's history including the parts that are hard to tell.
culture.bonus: Sit through the Story of the Forest digital installation on the way in.

culture.title: Peranakan Museum on Armenian Street
culture.description: A reopened museum of Straits-Chinese life — beadwork, wedding chambers, kitchens — in a 1912 school building, done at exactly the right scale.
culture.bonus: Study one embroidered wedding panel long enough to spot the mistakes.

culture.title: National Gallery in the Old Supreme Court
culture.description: Two linked colonial landmarks — City Hall and the Supreme Court — holding the world's largest public collection of Southeast Asian art.
culture.bonus: Find the old holding cells and the rooftop, both easy to walk straight past.

culture.title: Sultan Mosque and Kampong Glam
culture.description: A gold-domed 1928 mosque at the head of Bussorah Street, with the old Malay royal quarter, textile shops and Haji Lane all radiating off it.
culture.bonus: Walk Arab Street for fabric first, then the mosque, then Haji Lane.

chill.title: Sunset on Palawan Beach's Suspension Bridge
chill.description: A swaying rope bridge off Sentosa's south shore to two small towers billed as the southernmost point of continental Asia.
chill.bonus: Cross it, climb both towers, and watch the tankers from the top.

chill.title: Rain Vortex and Canopy Park at Jewel
chill.description: A 40-metre indoor waterfall falling through the middle of an airport, ringed by four storeys of forest, with a mirror maze and net walks on the roof.
chill.bonus: Go up to the Canopy Bridge and stand on the glass floor over the vortex.

chill.title: Pastries at Tiong Bahru Bakery
chill.description: Proper laminated viennoiserie in the middle of a 1930s estate, from the bakery that made Singaporeans queue for croissants in the first place.
chill.bonus: Get the kouign-amann and eat it on the steps outside while it's still warm.

chill.title: Morning Quiet at Thian Hock Keng
chill.description: Singapore's oldest Hokkien temple, built in 1839 without a single nail, on the street where immigrants came ashore to give thanks for the crossing.
chill.bonus: Walk round the back to the mural of the Hokkien migration story.

chill.title: Picnic Under Fort Canning's Tree Tunnel
chill.description: A colonial hill fort turned park in the middle of town, with a spiral stairwell framed by a ring of trees that has become the city's most photographed doorway.
chill.bonus: Get to the tree tunnel before eight to have it to yourself for one photo.

chill.title: Bumboat Down the Singapore River
chill.description: A converted wooden cargo boat from Clarke Quay past the godowns, the Fullerton and the Merlion to Marina Bay, with the skyline lighting up as you go.
chill.bonus: Sit at the back where the engine is and skip the narration entirely.

chill.title: Coffee and Shophouses in Tiong Bahru
chill.description: Singapore's oldest housing estate: curved 1930s art deco walk-ups, a wet market, an independent bookshop and no tall buildings anywhere in sight.
chill.bonus: Find the air raid shelter on Guan Chuan Street and read the plaque.

chill.title: Sunset from the Marina Bay Sands SkyPark
chill.description: The observation deck 57 floors up on the cantilevered end of the boat, looking down the length of the CBD and out over the anchored ships.
chill.bonus: Stay up for the 8pm Spectra show and watch it from directly above.

chill.title: Garden Rhapsody and the Cloud Forest
chill.description: The Supertree light-and-sound show at the top of the hour, bookended by a 35-metre indoor mountain wrapped in mist and a waterfall you stand inside.
chill.bonus: Lie flat on the ground under the Supertrees for the show. Everyone else stands.

chill.title: National Orchid Garden at the Botanic Gardens
chill.description: A thousand species and two thousand hybrids inside a UNESCO-listed 160-year-old garden, including the cool house of highland orchids.
chill.bonus: Find the orchid named after someone you've actually heard of.

social.title: Craft Beer Crawl in Tanjong Pagar
social.description: Shophouse after shophouse of taprooms and izakayas in the old docklands quarter, all within a few blocks of Tanjong Pagar MRT.
social.bonus: One drink per venue, five venues, no repeats, no taxis.

social.title: The Gin Tower at Atlas
social.description: An art deco cathedral of a bar in the lobby of the building locals call Gotham, with a 26-foot brass tower holding 1,300 gins.
social.bonus: Ask the bartender to pick a gin from the highest shelf they can reach.

social.title: Teepees and Skyline at Mr Stork
social.description: Level 39 of the Andaz, open-air, with ten thatched teepee huts and a 360-degree view that takes in Kampong Glam and the whole CBD.
social.bonus: Claim a teepee before sunset — there are only ten and they go fast.

social.title: No-Menu Cocktails at Bar Stories
social.description: A Haji Lane walk-up where there is no drinks list at all: you describe a mood and a bartender builds to it in front of you.
social.bonus: Give the bartender one word and nothing else to work with.

social.title: Find the Unmarked Door at 28 HongKong Street
social.description: No sign, no frontage, just a shophouse facade and a reservation — and behind it one of the most influential bars in Asia since 2011.
social.bonus: Sit at the bar, not a table, and let them build something off-menu.

social.title: Cocktails at Jigger & Pony
social.description: Singapore's most decorated bar, tucked into the Amara in Tanjong Pagar, with a drinks list bound like a magazine and service that never slips.
social.bonus: Order something you can't pronounce off the back pages of the menu.

social.title: Night Market Crawl at Bugis Street
social.description: Three floors of stalls and street food in the most chaotic market in the city centre, open late and cheap enough to buy things you don't need.
social.bonus: Haggle for something under five dollars and actually walk away once.

social.title: Three Floors and a Slide at Marquee
social.description: A 2,300 square metre club under the Shoppes at Marina Bay Sands with 70-foot ceilings, an eight-armed indoor Ferris wheel and a three-storey spiral slide.
social.bonus: Ride the Ferris wheel and take the slide down at least once.

social.title: Spectra from the Lantern Rooftop
social.description: The Fullerton Bay's sixth-floor rooftop, framed by an infinity pool, sitting directly across the water from the Marina Bay Sands light show.
social.bonus: Be in place for the 8pm show with a drink already in your hand.

social.title: Asian-Only Spirits at Native
social.description: Three floors of an Amoy Street shophouse — restaurant, bar, fermentation lab — pouring cocktails built only from regional spirits and foraged ingredients.
social.bonus: Order the one with ants in it and ask where they came from.

social.title: Riverside Crawl Along Clarke Quay
social.description: Restored godowns on both banks of the Singapore River, packed with bars, and a walk between them that takes about ninety seconds.
social.bonus: Start upstream at Robertson Quay and work your way down to Boat Quay.

social.title: Beer ATM at Little Island Brewing
social.description: A 400-seat brewery and smokehouse at sleepy Changi Village where you tap your card at a wall of taps and pour your own by the millilitre.
social.bonus: Pour five different beers in tiny measures instead of one pint.

8ball.title: Wildcard: Hawker Centre Roulette
8ball.description: Pick a hawker centre none of you have been to, then each order from the stall with the longest queue — no discussion, no looking at what it is first.
8ball.bonus: Eat everything you ordered. All of it. No trading.

8ball.title: Wildcard: Ride the Line to the End
8ball.description: Get on the MRT at City Hall, take whichever line comes first to its final station, and eat wherever you can walk to in ten minutes.
8ball.bonus: Ask someone at the terminus where they'd eat, then go there instead.

adventure.title: Cable Car from Mount Faber to Sentosa
adventure.description: A glass-floored gondola off the top of Mount Faber that crosses the harbour, the container terminal and Sentosa's canopy on one ticket.
adventure.bonus: Ride the Sentosa Line too and get off at Imbiah for the long walk down.

adventure.title: Cycle East Coast Park to Changi Point
adventure.description: 15km of flat seafront path from the reclaimed beaches of East Coast to the kampong end of the island, with container ships parked on the horizon the whole way.
adventure.bonus: Finish with a beer at Changi Village and take the bus back with the bike.

adventure.title: Night Luge Down Sentosa's Dragon Trail
adventure.description: Four gravity tracks down Imbiah Lookout on a steerable cart, run after dark under LED lighting with a Skyride chairlift back up each time.
adventure.bonus: Take the Skyride up with your feet off the bar and look back at the harbour.

adventure.title: Indoor Freefall at AltitudeX Sentosa
adventure.description: A vertical wind tunnel on Siloso Beach Walk that holds you in a 200km/h column of air with the South China Sea through the glass behind you.
adventure.bonus: Ask the instructor for the high-fly at the end and go up the full tube.

adventure.title: TreeTop Walk at MacRitchie Reservoir
adventure.description: A 250-metre free-standing suspension bridge strung between the two highest points of MacRitchie, 25 metres above old-growth rainforest with long-tailed macaques for company.
adventure.bonus: Do the full 11km loop clockwise so you hit the bridge before the crowds.

adventure.title: Walk the Coney Island Boardwalk
adventure.description: A deliberately undeveloped island off Punggol, 50 hectares of casuarina and coastal forest on gravel paths, with a resident wild cow nobody can quite explain.
adventure.bonus: Find the beach areas on the north shore and have the sea entirely to yourself.

adventure.title: Night Safari After Dark
adventure.description: The world's first nocturnal zoo, walked and tram-ridden after sunset through open habitats where the animals are actually awake.
adventure.bonus: Skip the tram on your second loop and walk the Leopard Trail alone.

adventure.title: HydroDash at Palawan Beach
adventure.description: Singapore's biggest floating obstacle course, 60 by 61 metres of inflatable slides, walls and monkey bars anchored in the Palawan lagoon.
adventure.bonus: Get across the whole course once without falling in. Good luck.

adventure.title: Sunrise and Kites at Marina Barrage
adventure.description: A grass rooftop over the dam that holds back the Marina Reservoir, where Singaporeans fly kites at dawn with the whole skyline standing behind them.
adventure.bonus: Bring breakfast and a cheap kite and stay until the heat drives you off.

adventure.title: Walk the Rail Corridor from Bukit Timah
adventure.description: 24km of former Malayan railway line turned green spine, walked from the restored Bukit Timah station through jungle, truss bridges and back gardens.
adventure.bonus: Find the black-and-white truss bridge over Bukit Timah Road and stand under it.

adventure.title: Cross Henderson Waves on the Southern Ridges
adventure.description: A rippling timber wave of a bridge 36 metres above Henderson Road, on a 10km green corridor that links Mount Faber to Kent Ridge without touching a pavement.
adventure.bonus: Time it so you're on the bridge as the deck lighting comes on at seven.

adventure.title: Mountain Bike Pulau Ubin's Ketam Trail
adventure.description: A bumboat to a kampong island ten minutes from the mainland, then a graded singletrack loop through old granite quarries and secondary jungle on a rented bike.
adventure.bonus: Ride out to Chek Jawa's wetlands boardwalk before you hand the bike back.

adventure.title: Mudflats and Mangroves at Sungei Buloh
adventure.description: A mangrove wetland reserve on the Johor Strait with hides, boardwalks, mudskippers and estuarine crocodiles that genuinely do turn up.
adventure.bonus: Stand still at a hide for ten full minutes and count what appears.

adventure.title: Dawn Climb to Bukit Timah's Summit
adventure.description: The highest natural point in Singapore at 163 metres, reached on a steep paved road through primary rainforest older than the city around it.
adventure.bonus: Take the Dairy Farm side trails down instead of the road you came up.

adventure.title: MegaZip Over the Sentosa Jungle
adventure.description: 450 metres of zipline at 60km/h from Imbiah Hill out over the treetops and down to a landing island off Siloso Beach.
adventure.bonus: Go tandem and try to beat the person next to you off the platform.

adventure.title: Kayak MacRitchie at the Paddle Lodge
adventure.description: Flat brown water, a rainforest shoreline and no motors allowed, paddled out of the reservoir's own boathouse before the afternoon storms build.
adventure.bonus: Paddle into the far arm of the reservoir until you can't hear the road.

foodie.title: Chilli Crab at Jumbo, East Coast
foodie.description: A whole mud crab in sweet-hot tomato gravy at the open-air seafood centre where the dish was perfected, with fried mantou buns to mop the plate.
foodie.bonus: Order the black pepper crab as well and settle the argument yourself.

foodie.title: Kaya Toast at Chin Mee Chin
foodie.description: A 1925 Katong bakery with mosaic floors and marble tables, where charcoal-toasted bread comes with coconut jam, cold butter and soft-boiled eggs.
foodie.bonus: Dip the toast in the egg with white pepper and soy, properly, no shortcuts.

foodie.title: Satay Street at Lau Pa Sat
foodie.description: At seven each evening Boon Tat Street closes to traffic and ten charcoal satay stalls set up in the road beside a Victorian cast-iron market hall.
foodie.bonus: Order fifty sticks between you and don't stop until the peanut sauce is gone.

foodie.title: Laksa at 328 Katong
foodie.description: Thick coconut gravy, cockles and noodles cut short so you eat the whole bowl with a spoon — the Katong original on East Coast Road, walk-ins only.
foodie.bonus: Add the otah on the side and eat it straight out of the banana leaf.

foodie.title: One-Star Bak Chor Mee at Hill Street Tai Hwa
foodie.description: Minced pork noodles with dried plaice, pork liver and black vinegar, cooked bowl by bowl at a Crawford Lane stall that has held a Michelin star since 2016.
foodie.bonus: Get there before ten or budget an hour in the queue — everyone does.

foodie.title: Tian Tian Chicken Rice at Maxwell
foodie.description: The most argued-over plate of Hainanese chicken rice in Singapore, poached since 1986 at a Maxwell Food Centre stall with a queue that starts before it opens.
foodie.bonus: Order the chilli extra and the dark soy on the side, like the regulars do.

foodie.title: Peranakan Tasting Menu at Candlenut
foodie.description: The world's first Michelin-starred Peranakan restaurant, in a Dempsey bungalow, where Malcolm Lee cooks buah keluak and rempah with restraint.
foodie.bonus: Take the Ah-Ma-Kase and let the kitchen decide the whole meal.

foodie.title: Prata Marathon at Springleaf Prata Place
foodie.description: Twenty variations on roti prata, flipped to order and eaten with fish curry — a Michelin-listed local chain that does murtabak properly too.
foodie.bonus: Order the plaster prata with a runny egg and don't ask about the calories.

foodie.title: 2am Dim Sum at Swee Choon
foodie.description: A Jalan Besar institution since 1962 that serves har gow and mee sua kueh until four in the morning, now finally open seven days a week.
foodie.bonus: Go after midnight, order the mee sua kueh, and watch who else turns up.

foodie.title: Barbecue Stingray at Newton Food Centre
foodie.description: Sambal stingray off the grill on banana leaf, fried carrot cake and sugarcane juice at the open-air hawker centre that made it onto every film crew's list.
foodie.bonus: Order from at least four different stalls and share everything at one table.

foodie.title: Nasi Lemak at The Coconut Club
foodie.description: Coconut rice cooked with a specific varietal, sambal with real depth and a fried chicken thigh — the Bib Gourmand version of Singapore's default lunch, on Beach Road.
foodie.bonus: Add the buah keluak if it's on and see what all the fuss is about.

foodie.title: Michelin Chicken Rice at Hawker Chan
foodie.description: The Chinatown Complex stall that became the cheapest Michelin-starred meal on earth: soya sauce chicken over rice for under five dollars.
foodie.bonus: Eat at the original non-air-conditioned hawker stall, not the shop next door.
